items.prompt_text: When the price of coffee rises from $4 to $5, the quantity demanded falls from 200 to 190 cups/day. Using the simple percentage-change method (changes relative to the initial values), what is the price elasticity of demand, as a positive decimal? Reply with just the number (e.g. 0.5).
items.reasoning: We need price elasticity of demand using simple percentage change method, relative to initial values. That is: % change in quantity demanded / % change in price. Use initial values. Price change: from 4 to 5. Initial price = 4. ΔP = 5-4 = 1. % change in price = ΔP / initial P = 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%. Quantity change: from 200 to 190. Initial Q = 200. ΔQ = 190-200 = -10. % change in Q = -10/200 = -0.05 = -5%. So elasticity = (-0.05)/(0.25) = -0.2. Positive decimal means take absolute value: 0.2. So answer: 0.2.
